title: In characteristic p, N-2 is tested on finite purely inseparable extensions
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] integral domain whose field of fractions $K$ has characteristic $p>0$. Suppose that for every finite purely inseparable field extension $L/K$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] (a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] with $\dim_K L<\infty$ such that every $\alpha\in L$ satisfies $\alpha^{p^n}\in K$ for some $n\ge0$) the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $R$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]: for every finite field extension $L/K$ the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ is a finitely generated $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032N (lemma-domain-char-p-N-1-2, line 45382), direction 'if' (the converse is immediate from the definition); tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Let $L/K$ be a finite field extension; write $A_L\subseteq L$ for the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-in-finite-normal-extension] there is a field extension $M/L$ with $M/K$ finite and normal; let $\iota:L\to M$ be the inclusion and $A_M\subseteq M$ the integral closure of $R$ in $M$. If $x\in A_L$ satisfies $x^n+r_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\dots+r_0=0$ with $r_i\in R$, applying the ring homomorphism $\iota$ (which is the identity on the image of $R$, since $R\to M$ factors as $R\to K\to L\to M$) gives the same equation for $\iota(x)$, so $\iota(A_L)\subseteq A_M$. As $\iota$ is injective and $R$-linear, $A_L\cong\iota(A_L)$ is isomorphic to an $R$-submodule of $A_M$. Hence, $R$ being Noetherian, if $A_M$ is a finitely generated $R$-module then so is $A_L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. It therefore suffices to show that $A_M$ is a finitely generated $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 032N (lemma-domain-char-p-N-1-2, lines 45389-45407), 'Choose a finite normal field extension M/K containing L. As R is Noetherian it suffices to show that the integral closure of R in M is finite over R'

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-purely-inseparable-then-galois] to the normal algebraic extension $M/K$ ($M/K$ is finite, so every element of $M$ is algebraic over $K$): the subfield $M_{insep}=M^{\mathrm{Aut}(M/K)}$ satisfies $K\subseteq M_{insep}\subseteq M$, $M_{insep}/K$ is purely inseparable, and $M/M_{insep}$ is separable algebraic. Moreover $M_{insep}/K$ is finite, being a $K$-subspace of the finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $M$, and $M/M_{insep}$ is finite, since a $K$-basis of $M$ spans $M$ over $M_{insep}\supseteq K$. By the hypothesis applied to the finite purely inseparable extension $M_{insep}/K$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], the integral closure $R'$ of $R$ in $M_{insep}$ is a finitely generated $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 032N (lemma-domain-char-p-N-1-2, lines 45389-45407), 'By Fields, Lemma 030M there exists a subextension M/M_insep/K such that M_insep/K is purely inseparable, and M/M_insep is separable. By assumption the integral closure R' of R in M_insep is finite over R'

proof.text: The ring $R'$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] ($R$ is Noetherian and $R'$ is a finitely generated $R$-module by step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], applied to the domain $R$ with fraction field $K$ and the finite extension $M_{insep}/K$, $R'$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and the inclusion $R'\subseteq M_{insep}$ identifies $M_{insep}$ with the fraction field of $R'$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 032N (lemma-domain-char-p-N-1-2, lines 45389-45407), the hypotheses of Lemma 032L for R' (Noetherian normal domain with fraction field M_insep), which the source uses without comment

proof.text: By steps 2 and 3, $R'$ is a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $M_{insep}$ and $M/M_{insep}$ is a finite separable algebraic extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] the integral closure $R''$ of $R'$ in $M$ is a finitely generated $R'$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-over-finite-algebra], applied to $R\to R'\to R''$, $R''$ is a finitely generated $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 032N (lemma-domain-char-p-N-1-2, lines 45389-45407), 'By Lemma 032L the integral closure R'' of R' in M is finite over R'. Then R'' is finite over R by Lemma 00GL'

proof.text: Let C be the integral closure of R' in M. An element integral over R is integral over R' by mapping its monic equation along R to R' (Mathlib IsIntegral.tower_top). Thus the identity on M restricts to an injective R-linear map from the integral closure of R in M to C. By step 4 C is finite over R, and R is Noetherian, so Module.Finite.of_injective (lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite) gives finiteness of the integral closure of R in M. The reverse inclusion and transitivity of integrality are unnecessary.

proof.text: By steps 1 and 5, for every finite field extension $L/K$ the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ is a finitely generated $R$-module; this is the definition of $R$ being N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].
